method: Review public non-merge history for six months, including runtime, installer, packaging and CI defects. Candidate selection uses fix/repair/security-related subjects plus manual additions after reading the complete subject history. Ordinary dependency updates without an identified project defect are not bugs. Individual commits can bundle multiple defects; the provisional group counts below are not the criterion denominator. Later regression evidence is allowed when dated accurately. Missing links mean unverified, not proof of absent tests.

defect_review.method: Manual review of each candidate diff, split by independent failure mechanism. New source-bound release-note functionality and its first implementation tests are not counted as historical defects. Repeated attempts to repair one cause and empty/format-only commits are explicitly excluded. Existing later tests count only where their assertions address the old defect; tests without an exact verified link conservatively do not count in the numerator. Earlier group-level discovery data is retained for traceability, not used as the denominator.
defect_review.reviewed_scope: Non-merge main history from 2026-04-12 through initial inspected head, plus current reviewed PR fixes. Changes were classified by failure mechanism, not one test or one commit per bug.

representative_replay.method: Use the fix commit checkout and its exact test; substitute only affected source with the parent version. Run isolated pytest without coverage.
representative_replay.assertion: After a wall-clock rollback and six elapsed monotonic seconds the parent returns None; fixed reader reconnects and returns 75.
representative_replay.limitations: Historical fix checkout uses its historical tests/configuration in the current interpreter. It is a controlled affected-source substitution, not a complete historical build environment.
